question.text: If the equation $x^{2}-ca+d=0$ has roots equal to the fourth powers of the roots of $x^{2}+a x+b=0,$ where $a^{2}>4 b,$ then the roots of $x^{2}-4 b x+2 b^{2}-c=0$ will be

solution.text:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^{2}+a x+b=0$ and the roots of $x^{2}-cx+d=0$ are $\alpha^{4}$ and $\beta^{4}$
Now, $\alpha+\beta=-a, \alpha \beta=b$ ...(i)
and $\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}-c, \alpha^{4} \beta^{4}=d$ ...(ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$b^{4}=d$ and $\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}=c$
$\left(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}\right)^{2}-2(\alpha \beta)^{2}=c$
$\left.\Rightarrow \quad\left[(\alpha+\beta)^{2}-2 \alpha \beta\right]^{2}-2 (\alpha\beta\right)^{2}=c$
$\Rightarrow \quad\left(a^{2}-2 b\right)^{2}-2 b^{2}=c$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 b^{2}+c=\left(a^{2}-2 b\right)^{2}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 b^{2}+c=a^{4}+4 b^{2}-4 a^{2} b$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 b^{2}-c=4 a^{2} b-a^{4}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 b^{2}-c=a^{2}\left(4 b-a^{2}\right)$
and for equation $x^{2}-4 b x+2 b^{2}-c=0$
$$
D=(4 b)^{2}-4(1)\left(2 b^{2}-c\right)
$$
$=16 b^{2}-8 b^{2}+4 c=8 b^{2}+4 c$
$=4\left(2 b^{2}+c\right)=4\left(a^{2}-2 b\right)^{2}>0=$ real root
Now, $f(0)=2 b^{2}-c=a^{2}\left(4 b-a^{2}\right)    < 0 \quad\left(\because a^{2}>4 b\right)$
= roots are opposite in sign
